H2.why: Better structure: one home per fact, plan 46% shorter, design has no restated summary, W1/W2 modelled, all what-ifs reproduce. Worse substance for a manager: phase 1 no longer creates Jira tickets (r6 did, in the same capacity), and the lead walkthrough and hosted quality check are gone. 'Fits' rests on zero handoff hours. Still 43% over budget, mostly waste: the design (3,800 words) is written at production granularity, with an 11-row decision table with long cells, a 13-row depth table plus a separate deferred table, and failure rows for phase-2 Jira paths.

H4.why: Same length (+25%). W1 is modelled correctly, the runbook drill and staging rollback are back, every quoted figure reproduces. But the headline remedy (Dev A at 6 h) fails if G03's review is done by Dev B as the plan says. The 'only Dev A hours' negative claim is false, the overflow suggestion is contradicted, 5 handoffs have no hours, and the pass bar and partial-move row were lost. The over-budget part is mostly a 7-row change-history table and phase-2 yaml entries: waste for a manager.

H5.why: Design+plan down 33% to 9,048 (13% over 8,000). Summary is accurate, six day-1 waits are modelled with a request list, the sandbox wait is conservative again, and the r6 contradictions about load share and 'a week' are gone. Remaining issues: the 'not by hours' / 'spare hours don't help' claims are false; G12's missing dependencies would push the finish to 103.8 days and defeat both remedies; there are zero handoff hours (which also defeat the +2-day remedy); and the AI-notice acceptance was lost. The over-budget part is mostly justified (the decision and guarantee tables carry the production floor), with ~250 words of yaml boilerplate and phase-2 hour splits as waste.

top_issues: Handoff hours remain the most common gap: H2 0 of 1, H4 1 of 6, H5 0 of many. In H2 and H5 adding them changes the verdict or defeats a remedy

Negative and comparative claims are still not tested against the helper (H4 'only Dev A hours'; H5 'not by hours' / 'spare hours don't shorten the chain'). Goal splits and other people's hours close the gap in both
